title.narrative: Improving social sustainability in the granite supply chain, South India (SSF24S003)

description.narrative: This project is a collaboration between Den Hollandsche and Stichting Local Impact Hub from the Netherlands and Granite Products Corporation, MV Foundation and Paradigm Shift from India. It focuses on the granite quarries in five locations in South India. Each location gives a specific pattern and color, the quarries are chosen based on this stone characteristics. Around 30 quarries supply granite in this supply chain. The locations of the quarries are in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka Province. The beneficiaries of this project are the workers in the quarries and factories in the granite supply chain.The project focusses in eradication of child labour from the granite production in this supply chain. The risk of child labour is most prominent in the quarries, especially with children over 15 years old and for migrants. Working conditions in the factory and the quarries are a high risk in all parts of the supply chain. In the quarries the risks are higher, also since there are quite of lot of migrant workers, and contracted workers in the quarries. The project focusses at identifying the working risks and labour rights risks, in order to mitigate these risks and diminish them in phase B. Living wage is the third relevant sustainability issue our project focusses on, the minimum wage in India is set by the government, and all companies uphold to this wage. Often quarry workers are hired through a contractor. The project partners will investigate the types of contract forms in quarries and factory and the income strategies of the workers families in order to assess how and where income improvements towards living income can be made. In phase B they will focus their activities and interventions on the risks that are most prominent from the risk assessment.
